blocks.heading: Environmental-quality assessment
blocks.text:
An environmental-quality assessment records selected conditions using a defined scoring scale. For a tourism investigation, conditions might include litter, noise, vegetation damage and waste facilities. State whether higher scores mean better or worse quality. Use the same indicators, category descriptions and observation period at each site so that totals can be compared. A score is an organised judgement, not a direct measurement of every environmental process.

![Environmental-quality assessment sheet with its recording procedure](../../assets/images/ITEM-6137-2.3-036-PROC-answer.png)

blocks.text: The usual recording sheet is a bi-polar grid. Each row pairs a positive description with its opposite, such as “no litter” and “litter everywhere”, with a scale between them, for example +2, +1, 0, −1, −2. Choose rows that suit the hypothesis: litter, noise, trampled vegetation, congestion, condition of facilities. Put every positive description on the same side so that the row scores can be added into a site total.

Use enough sites to show a pattern: two sites cannot show a trend, so five or more, for example at set distances from a viewpoint or campsite, give more meaningful results. Survey every site at the same time of day, because noise, traffic and litter change through the day. Observers practise on one site first so that they read the descriptions alike.

Suppose a grid has five rows scored +2 to −2, so a site total can range from −10 to +10. A site beside a car park scores −1, −2, 0, −1, +1, a total of −3. A site 500 m away scores +2, +1, +1, +2, +1, a total of +7, showing better assessed quality. A simpler sheet scores each indicator from 0 (poor) to 2 (good).

Present the totals as a bar chart, or plot each site total against distance or visitor count. A profile graph of one site's row scores shows which indicators are poor. If totals of 6, 4 and 2 match visitor counts of 10, 30 and 50 while the facilities score stays at 2, quality falls with use but facilities did not decline.
